project.name: Tree Complete
project.description: Explore a program as a living tree of explicit, forkable design decisions.

decisions.title: Data boundary
decisions.question: Where does canonical project state live?
decisions.rationale: The source of truth controls offline behavior, collaboration cost, and how safely a fork can be reproduced.

alternatives.label: Local JSON ledger
alternatives.description: Keep a compact, inspectable state document beside the project.
alternatives.impact: Fast startup and simple recovery with single-writer semantics.

brief.objective: Use an atomically replaced JSON document as the canonical store.
constraints: Preserve a small typed storage boundary so another backend can be introduced later.
Keep runtime state inspectable and local to the Tree Complete data directory.
acceptance: Concurrent in-process mutations serialize and preserve every update.
Crash recovery reads either the previous or replacement state as one complete document.

alternatives.label: Embedded SQLite
alternatives.description: Persist normalized versions, decisions, and run events in SQLite.
alternatives.impact: Stronger queries and transactions at the cost of a binary dependency.

brief.objective: Replace the JSON persistence adapter with an embedded SQLite store.
constraints: Retain the existing public API and typed storage boundary.
Model versions, decisions, alternatives, runs, and logs transactionally.
acceptance: A single transaction publishes each complete workspace mutation.
Restart recovery preserves every committed version and terminal run.

alternatives.label: Append-only event log
alternatives.description: Derive current state by folding immutable domain events.
alternatives.impact: Excellent provenance and replay, with more projection machinery.

brief.objective: Represent every workspace mutation as an immutable event with deterministic projection.
constraints: Keep snapshots optional and disposable.
Retain the existing public workspace and fork API.
acceptance: Replaying the same ordered event stream produces an identical workspace.
After an interrupted write, every earlier event remains intact and replayable.

decisions.title: Execution isolation
decisions.question: How should generated forks be isolated from the source checkout?
decisions.rationale: Agents need real files and Git history, while unfinished experiments must stay out of the working branch.

alternatives.label: Git worktree
alternatives.description: Give every fork a dedicated branch and linked checkout.
alternatives.impact: Low disk overhead, native diffs, and immediately inspectable output.

brief.objective: Create each generated version in a dedicated Git worktree rooted at its exact parent commit.
constraints: Use sanitized, collision-resistant branch names.
Keep the source checkout files unchanged and retain failed worktrees for diagnosis.
acceptance: The generated commit has the recorded parent commit as its sole parent.
The recorded fork branch resolves to the generated commit.

alternatives.label: Ephemeral clone
alternatives.description: Clone the repository into a fully independent directory per run.
alternatives.impact: Clear isolation with higher setup and storage cost.

brief.objective: Replace linked worktrees with local clones that are pinned to each fork's parent commit.
constraints: Create a dedicated sanitized branch in every clone.
Preserve the existing run lifecycle and lineage API.
acceptance: After each run, the source repository's worktree and local branch refs exactly match their initial state.
The result exposes a verifiable commit and inspectable repository location.

alternatives.label: Disposable container
alternatives.description: Execute each coding run inside a constrained container.
alternatives.impact: Stronger process isolation but substantially more orchestration.

brief.objective: Run generation and inspection inside a disposable rootless container.
constraints: Mount only the fork checkout and narrowly required credentials.
Apply explicit process, memory, time, filesystem, and network limits.
acceptance: The generated Git commit is the container's only durable program result.
After timeout or termination, every process started for the run has exited.

decisions.title: Agent feedback
decisions.question: How much execution detail should the interface expose?
decisions.rationale: Useful progress builds trust, but raw model output is noisy and can disclose repository details.

alternatives.label: Curated phases
alternatives.description: Show stable phases, progress, and short orchestration messages.
alternatives.impact: Readable and safe, while retaining enough evidence to diagnose failures.

brief.objective: Present a curated run timeline with queued, preparing, generating, inspecting, and terminal phases.
constraints: Store bounded human-readable orchestration messages instead of raw agent output.
Keep terminal success and failure states durable across refreshes.
acceptance: Every active run exposes a monotonic phase and bounded progress value.
Client-visible logs disclose neither raw subprocess output nor secrets.

alternatives.label: Live terminal stream
alternatives.description: Stream sanitized subprocess output into a terminal-style panel.
alternatives.impact: Maximum immediacy with redaction, backpressure, and retention concerns.

brief.objective: Add a bounded server-sent event stream for sanitized agent output.
constraints: Apply backpressure and redact secrets and absolute paths before publication.
Retain only a concise terminal summary after the live run.
acceptance: Per-client buffering stays within a fixed bound for slow or disconnected clients.
Stream and persisted output pass deterministic redaction tests.

alternatives.label: Result only
alternatives.description: Keep a run quiet until a commit or failure is available.
alternatives.impact: Minimal interface noise, but long runs appear inert.

brief.objective: Collapse active feedback into a single pending state and publish only the terminal result.
constraints: Preserve detailed internal diagnostics in bounded server logs.
Keep the public terminal failure normalized and safe to display.
acceptance: The client receives only the terminal result.
Completion publishes the result commit summary and failure publishes a concise reason.

decisions.title: Verification policy
decisions.question: What evidence is required before a generated fork is complete?
decisions.rationale: A branch existing is weaker evidence than a focused change that passes the project's own checks.

alternatives.label: Targeted checks
alternatives.description: Ask the agent to run checks relevant to the edited surface, then inspect the staged diff.
alternatives.impact: Good signal-to-runtime balance across unfamiliar repositories.

brief.objective: Derive inspection from the changed surface and the repository's existing project commands.
constraints: Run focused tests and static checks relevant to the change.
Require a non-empty, whitespace-clean staged diff before the host commit.
acceptance: Codex is explicitly instructed to run focused checks and resolve failures caused by its change.
Public result evidence distinguishes host-enforced Git integrity from unverified agent activity.
The host rejects an empty or whitespace-invalid generated diff.

alternatives.label: Full project suite
alternatives.description: Run every declared project check for every generated fork.
alternatives.impact: Higher confidence when suites are reliable, with slower feedback.

brief.objective: Discover and run the repository's canonical complete validation workflow before commit.
constraints: Use only project-declared validation surfaces.
Record failed check names as structured diagnostics.
acceptance: Every declared project check exits successfully before the fork completes.
Publication follows successful completion of every declared check.

alternatives.label: Agent review council
alternatives.description: Have independent agents test and adversarially review the implementation.
alternatives.impact: Broad semantic scrutiny at materially greater compute and latency.

brief.objective: Invoke independent test and adversarial-review agents after implementation.
constraints: Keep reviewer contexts independent before reconciliation.
Fix confirmed findings before the host creates the result commit.
acceptance: Both reviewers produce structured evidence tied to the generated diff.
The final run records how every confirmed finding was resolved.
